name: Question 14
problem: A snowball is rolling down a snow-covered hillside. At a particular moment, the rate of increase in the volume of the sphere is numerically equal to three times the rate of increase in its surface area. What is the radius of the sphere at that moment?
worked_solution:
Let $r$ be the radius of the sphere, $V$ the volume of the sphere, and $A$ its surface area. We wish to find $r$ at the moment when $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=3\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.$

To start, let's set up an equation relating the volume $V$ and the surface area $A$ of the sphere. Since $A=4\pi {r}^{2}$ and $V=\frac{4\pi }{3}{r}^{3},$ the relationship between $V$ and $A$ is

$$
V=\frac{4\pi }{3}{r}^{3}=\frac{4\pi }{3}{(\frac{A}{4\pi })}^{3/2}=\frac{{A}^{3/2}}{3(4\pi )^{1/2}}=\frac{{A}^{3/2}}{6\sqrt{\pi }}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{A}^{3/2}}{6\sqrt{\pi }}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}A}(\frac{{A}^{3/2}}{6\sqrt{\pi }}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{{A}^{1/2}}{4\sqrt{\pi }}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=3\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{{A}^{1/2}}{4\sqrt{\pi }} \\ {A}^{1/2} & =12\sqrt{\pi } \\ A & ={(12\sqrt{\pi })}^{2} \\ A & =144\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, since $A=4\pi {r}^{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4\pi {r}^{2} & =144\pi  \\ {r}^{2} & =36 \\ r & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

A snowball is rolling down a snow-covered hillside. At a particular moment, the rate of increase in the volume of the sphere is numerically equal to three times the rate of increase in its surface area. What is the radius of the sphere at that moment?

a
 4
b
 4π
c
6π
d
 6
e
 3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let r be the radius of the sphere, V the volume of the sphere, and A its surface area. We wish to find r at the moment when dVdt=3dAdt.

To start, let's set up an equation relating the volume V and the surface area A of the sphere. Since A=4πr2 and V=4π3r3, the relationship between V and A is

V=4π3r3=4π3(A4π)3/2=A3/23(4π)1/2=A3/26π.

Differentiating this relationship with respect to t using implicit differentiation, we get

ddt(V)=ddt(A3/26π)dVdt=dAdt⋅ddA(A3/26π)dVdt=dAdt⋅A1/24π.

Now, since dVdt=3dAdt, we have

3dAdt=dAdt⋅A1/24πA1/2=12πA=(12π)2A=144π.

Lastly, since A=4πr2, we have

4πr2=144πr2=36r=6.
